html:
The Kutadgu Bilig, "the wisdom that brings good fortune", is a long poem of advice to rulers written around 1069 by Yusuf of Balasagun. It is one of the earliest masterpieces of Turkic literature.

Yusuf came from Balasagun, a city in today's Kyrgyzstan, and presented the poem to the ruler of the Kara-Khanids in Kashgar. In return he was given the title Khass Hajib, "privy chamberlain".

The poem has more than six thousand couplets. It is built as a set of talks between four figures, each standing for an idea:

  • the king, who stands for justice
  • his vizier, good fortune
  • the vizier's son, intelligence
  • a hermit, the life of the soul that turns away from the world

Through their talks Yusuf discusses how to govern, how to behave at court, and how to balance this world and the next. He wrote in Turkic but drew on Persian books of advice for princes, and he used the same metre as the Shahnameh.

It was written at almost the same time as the Turkic dictionary of Mahmud al-Kashgari. Three manuscripts survive, in Vienna, Cairo and Namangan.
sum: The Kutadgu Bilig, "the wisdom that brings good fortune", is a long poem of advice to rulers written around 1069 by Yusuf of Balasagun. It is one of the earliest masterpieces of Turkic literature.
